metadata.title: Survey Identity and Anonymity

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for governing how respondent identity is handled, exposed, separated, or suppressed in surveys.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Survey identity handling mechanisms, respondent authentication services, tokenization layers, and anonymity enforcement logic.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Constraint pattern governing identity exposure, separation, and anonymity semantics in survey systems.

props.name: depends-on-pattern
props.remarks: Identity and anonymity constraints are applied to surveys governed under Survey Core.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Survey identity handling aligns with NIST SP 800-53 identity and privacy control families.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Survey anonymity and identity separation align with Privacy Framework principles for de-identification and minimization.

metadata.remarks: Survey Identity and Anonymity defines enforceable constraints on how respondent identity is handled in surveys. This pattern ensures that identity exposure is explicit, minimized, and consistent with declared anonymity models, preventing unintended attribution, correlation, or re-identification.

components.title: Identity Model Declaration
components.description: Requires surveys to explicitly declare whether they are anonymous, pseudonymous, or identifiable before participation.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Misrepresentation of survey anonymity or identity handling to influence participation.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Explicit disclosure and confirmation prevent ambiguity in identity expectations.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Individuals are informed of how their identity will be handled prior to participation.

components.title: Identity and Response Separation
components.description: Ensures that respondent identity is logically and technically separated from survey responses when anonymity or pseudonymity is promised.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Derivation of personal identity through correlation of survey responses with metadata.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Separation, tokenization, and minimization prevent re-identification.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Mechanisms prevent unauthorized association between identities and responses.

components.title: Identity Minimization
components.description: Limits collection of identity-related attributes to only those strictly required for stated survey purposes.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Over-collection of identity attributes beyond survey necessity.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Data minimization reduces identity exposure and correlation risk.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Only the minimum identity information necessary is collected.

components.title: Anonymity and Pseudonymity Enforcement
components.description: Ensures declared anonymity or pseudonymity properties cannot be bypassed or retroactively altered.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Use of legitimate access to improperly reveal or infer respondent identity.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Structural enforcement of anonymity guarantees prevents later disclosure.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Least privilege is applied to prevent identity disclosure.
Participation does not require identity exposure unless explicitly declared.
